MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA AUTOMATION ENGINEER | CI/CD & PLATFORM ENGINEERING
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has built Helm-based ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster. Personal hands-on experience with k3s, GitOps and Terraform complements professional platform-adjacent work. Currently studying for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam.

CORE SKILLS
CI/CD and automation: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm
Infrastructure and platforms: Kubernetes (namespace-level access; basic), k3s, Terraform (personal project), Argo CD, Linux
Monitoring and data: Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, PostgreSQL, SQL
Programming and scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Other: Git, Ansible (basic), AWS (EC2 and S3 basics; personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes through parallel test jobs, dependency caching and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; reduced monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral test environments using Docker Compose and later Helm charts deployed to the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a test-results pipeline and Grafana dashboards to show flaky tests by team.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
- Wrote the internal guide to CI pipelines used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications for client projects.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform in a personal account; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Delivered short-lived environments for each merge request, with the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity, enabling QA and product reviews before merge and end-to-end testing against each environment.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split end-to-end tests into a separate stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
- Helped teams identify and address leading flaky-test issues; the flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1%.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into CI/CD and platform-adjacent work. The strongest evidence is specific and quantified: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by about 30%, approximately 900 end-to-end tests maintained, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The ephemeral-environment and homelab projects add useful infrastructure evidence. The main content limitation is role alignment: the CV presents substantial CI/CD, Kubernetes application deployment and test-infrastructure experience, but less direct evidence of production cloud infrastructure ownership, systems architecture, networking, security or technical stakeholder leadership. The duplicated project descriptions also make the document somewhat longer than necessary.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: standard section headings, conventional chronology, searchable technology names, no tables or graphics, and clear employer and date formatting. It contains relevant terms such as Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, GitLab CI, Linux, monitoring, PostgreSQL, and TLS. ATS and AI screening for this particular role will likely be moderate rather than strong because the document does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, infrastructure security, cloud environment operation, or explicit technical proposal/stakeholder terminology. Those are genuine experience gaps or unsupported areas, not keywords that should be inserted without evidence. The use of both a detailed Professional Experience section and overlapping Selected Projects is useful for evidence but could be streamlined to improve scanability.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a credible adjacent or junior-to-mid platform/DevOps candidate, particularly for CI/CD, developer enablement, Kubernetes application environments, observability and automation. The CV shows hands-on infrastructure-adjacent work through Helm deployments to a shared Kubernetes cluster, GitLab CI ownership, Docker-based environments, k3s, GitOps, Terraform in a personal project, and monitoring with Prometheus/Grafana/Loki. It also shows analytical thinking, ownership and communication through quantified improvements, pipeline profiling, an internal onboarding guide, and mentoring. However, the role asks for strong Terraform and Terragrunt, cloud infrastructure design and operation, systems architecture, networking including mTLS, practical security, and leading technical proposals across stakeholders. The candidate's own material indicates no professional AWS/GCP/Azure experience, only basic personal AWS learning and a personal Hetzner/Terraform project; no Terragrunt; namespace-level rather than cluster-level Kubernetes access; and no stated mTLS, production on-call or train/IoT integration experience. The CV should therefore position the candidate accurately as an infrastructure/DevOps transition candidate with strong CI/CD and Kubernetes test-environment experience, rather than implying full equivalence to an experienced cloud infrastructure contractor.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None. The CV's claims are supported by the Original Candidate Information, and the CKA wording correctly states that the certification has not yet been obtained.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, make the infrastructure scope and strongest role-relevant evidence more immediately visible without overstating it. For example, replace the current summary with: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has built Helm-based environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster. Hands-on personal experience includes k3s, GitOps, observability and Terraform-based Hetzner infrastructure." Do not describe yourself as owning production cloud infrastructure or as a Terraform/Terragrunt specialist.
2. In the Core Skills section, separate professional experience from personal-project experience more clearly. For example, rename "Infrastructure and platforms" to "Infrastructure and platforms: Kubernetes (namespace-level access; basic), Helm, Linux" and add a separate line: "Personal projects: k3s, Argo CD, Terraform, Hetzner VPS, Ansible (basic), AWS EC2/S3 basics." This makes the evidence more credible and avoids implying that Terraform, AWS and Argo CD were used professionally.
3. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, make the technical ownership and stakeholder-facing effect of the ephemeral environments clearer. Revise the relevant bullet to: "Built merge-request ephemeral test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster, including the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity so QA and product teams could review changes before merge and run end-to-end tests against isolated environments." This uses evidence already present in the portfolio and better connects the work to developer enablement and collaboration.
4. In the same Odrava Health section, add the documented communication and technical-leadership evidence as separate bullets if space permits: "Wrote the internal guide to CI pipelines used for team onboarding" and "Mentored two QA interns in 2023." These are already supported by the candidate information and help address the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing others along without claiming formal infrastructure leadership.
5. In the Selected Projects section, reduce duplication with Professional Experience. Keep the four projects, but limit each Odrava project to two concise bullets and retain the detailed implementation evidence in the Odrava employment entry. This will make the CV easier to scan while preserving the strongest ATS terms and metrics.
6. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, make the TLS evidence precise and avoid implying broader networking or security expertise. Keep wording such as "configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS"; do not add mTLS, certificate-rotation, network-design or security claims because they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.
7. In the Certification and Professional Development section, retain the explicit status wording, but format it consistently as: "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — exam preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified)." This prevents automated or human readers from misinterpreting the item as an obtained certification.
